turns.user: my dumbbells only go up to 24kg each and bench is getting easy, should I just go to 40kg
turns.reply:
That is way too big a jump, Ashley — going from 24kg to 40kg per hand is a 16kg leap per side, which will wreck your form and put your shoulders at serious risk. 

When your dumbbells top out, you don't need heavier weights straight away to keep building. You can make 24kg feel significantly harder by adding a 3-second eccentric (lowering) phase, pausing for a second at the bottom, or adding reps and sets. That increases muscle tension without needing a massive jump in load.

If you're ready for heavier kit, the standard step up from 24kg is usually 26kg or 28kg. 

Where are you stalling on the bench right now — is it getting the 24s into position at the start, or are you flying through 12+ easy reps?

turns.user: so what do I actually do next week
turns.reply:
For next week, stick with your 24kg dumbbells and we'll change how you move them instead of adding weight.

Slow every rep down: take 3 seconds to lower the weight to your chest, pause for 1 second at the bottom, then drive up. That extra time under tension forces your chest to work much harder without needing heavier kit.

Aim for 3 sets of 8 to 10 reps with that tempo on Tuesday. Once you can hit 10 clean reps with the pause, we can talk about upgrading your dumbbells. Sound like a plan?
